title: CLOCK ALARMS DOWN TO A QUARTER

edits.replacement:
// v16.xx, his order: still too loud after v16.30 took them to a third; a quarter of that level again, .04 to .01
      cwg.gain.setValueAtTime(.01*vol,cwt); cwg.gain.setValueAtTime(.01*vol,cwt+.2);

edits.anchor: ckg.gain.setValueAtTime(.03*vol,t); ckg.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(.001,t+.09);   // v16.30: a third of the level
edits.replacement:
// v16.xx, his order: the last ten seconds tick goes down with the clock alarms, a quarter of the v16.30 level, .03 to .0075
    ckg.gain.setValueAtTime(.0075*vol,t); ckg.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(.001,t+.09);

why: The 5 minutes left alarm and every other clock mark (4, 3, 2, 1 minutes and 30 seconds) all play one sound, the clockwarn tone in blip (three rising triangle sweeps), and the last ten seconds play the clocktick knock; both are called with no distance, so the gain in the code is the level they play at. v16.30 did not halve them: git shows it cut the warning from .12 to .04 and the tick from .09 to .03, a third, and swapped the warning from a square to a softer triangle tone. He still finds them too loud, so this build cuts both to a quarter of the v16.30 level: the warning goes .04 to .01 and the tick .03 to .0075. Nothing else moves; the machine and pillager alarm stays at .06 and the check reads it as a control. The shape of the warning is untouched, so it still climbs like nothing else in the game. Both windows run the same code, so player 2 hears the same level as player 1.
